entry.title: DUNE construction
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. Construction of the Long-Baseline Neutrino Facility, which hosts DUNE, is entering its next phase, with critical components arriving and partner institutions contributing. UK teams have completed half of the 137 Anode Plane Assemblies, the sensors that detect the electrical signals from neutrino interactions in liquid argon. Black Hills State University has also joined the collaboration, which now counts more than 1,500 collaborators from 228 institutions in 38 countries and CERN.

entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. SLAC researchers developed SPINE, a machine-learning program that reconstructs neutrino interactions from complex detector images. It is currently deployed in neutrino experiments including the SBN programme and DUNE.

entry.title: KM3NeT and gravitational waves
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. KM3NeT published a paper on searches for coincident gravitational waves and high-energy neutrinos, using KM3NeT and ANTARES data from the O3 observing run. The motivation is that sources of gravitational waves may also produce high-energy neutrinos. Separately, the collaboration held its Autumn 2026 meeting in Siracusa, with status updates on detector operations on the agenda.

entry.title: IceCube activities
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. More than 230 participants attended the fall 2026 IceCube collaboration meeting in Madison, Wisconsin, which is held there every two years. At the South Pole, the winterovers spent the week of the 42nd-week report on detector maintenance and troubleshooting, including a hard-drive replacement and software updates, and calibration operations were under way on the Upgrade.

entry.title: Project 8 tritium source
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. Project 8 aims to measure the neutrino mass from tritium beta decay using cyclotron radiation emission spectroscopy, with a stated sensitivity goal of 40 meV/c^2. A new preprint describes a prototype electron cyclotron resonance dissociator, driven by a tunable 1 kW, 2.45 GHz RF generator and electromagnets, that ignites a hydrogen plasma. It is one stage of the planned beamline that dissociates molecular tritium.

entry.title: Auger sterile search
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The Pierre Auger Collaboration studies the observatory's sensitivity to sterile neutrinos of MeV-to-100 MeV mass in a 3+1 framework, with the sterile state mixing mainly with the tau flavour. Such neutrinos could cross long chords of the Earth and produce tau leptons that decay in the atmosphere and generate air showers. The exposures are computed with a detailed Monte Carlo simulation of neutrino propagation.

entry.title: CMS heavy neutral leptons
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. CMS reports a search for a Majorana heavy neutral lepton produced in top quark decays, in a type-I seesaw scenario. It uses 13 TeV proton-proton data from 2016 to 2018 corresponding to 138 fb^-1, and selects events with a same-sign, same-flavour lepton pair.

entry.title: NINJA FROST tracker
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. A meter-scale scintillator tracker, FROST, was built and operated in the NINJA experiment to match muon tracks between the nuclear emulsion detectors and the downstream muon detector. During J-PARC neutrino-beam operation it reached a data acquisition efficiency of 99.59% and a detection efficiency of 99.946±0.006% for selected neutrino-induced muons well within the active area.

The work is motivated by growing interest in detecting scintillation light at low temperature in bolometric experiments such as RES-NOVA and CUPID.

entry.title: The paper evaluates the neutrino emissivity of Δ-direct-Urca processes in neutron-star matter, a contribution
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper evaluates the neutrino emissivity of Δ-direct-Urca processes in neutron-star matter, a contribution the authors say had not been explicitly computed. It matters for neutron-star thermal evolution, where Urca processes are the dominant cooling mechanisms.

entry.title: The authors investigate whether kiloton-scale detectors such as Hyper-Kamiokande could determine the primary c
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The authors investigate whether kiloton-scale detectors such as Hyper-Kamiokande could determine the primary cosmic-ray spectrum from the atmospheric neutrino flux. They find that future detectors can distinguish cosmic-ray models with high statistical significance, even with uncertainties in neutrino cross sections and hadronic interactions. This connects atmospheric-neutrino measurements to a cosmic-ray input that is normally measured by satellites and balloons.

entry.title: Motivated by updated IceCube data for NGC 1068 extending down to about 0.2 TeV, the paper computes hadronic ne
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. Motivated by updated IceCube data for NGC 1068 extending down to about 0.2 TeV, the paper computes hadronic neutrino production and accompanying cascade gamma rays. It explores the parameter space with Latin hypercube sampling, constrained by multimessenger observations. It is relevant for what the neutrino data imply about conditions near the black hole.

entry.title: The paper presents semianalytic approximations for the quasisteady outcome of slow and fast flavour conversion
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper presents semianalytic approximations for the quasisteady outcome of slow and fast flavour conversion in neutrino-dense environments. The ansatz agrees well with multiangle and multienergy solutions of the kinetic equations, independently of the mass ordering. Such subgrid schemes matter because supernova hydrodynamic simulations cannot include neutrino quantum kinetics.

entry.title: The paper proves a no-go theorem for observing a Majorana phase in open two-flavour neutrino oscillations
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper proves a no-go theorem for observing a Majorana phase in open two-flavour neutrino oscillations. Any completely positive trace-preserving evolution covariant under rotations of the mass-coherence plane is exactly phase blind. A rate anisotropy can supply an environmental phase reference, which tells experimentalists what a decoherence environment would need to look like.

entry.title: The authors use solar neutrino-electron scattering data from PandaX-4T and XENONnT to constrain anomaly-free U
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The authors use solar neutrino-electron scattering data from PandaX-4T and XENONnT to constrain anomaly-free U(1)_X dark photon models with kinetic and mass mixing. They derive exclusion limits for six benchmark models and find that the stringency of the limits correlates with the leptonic charge assignments. It shows how dark-matter detectors double as neutrino-physics probes.
